clue.text: In bed is not as fortunate

indicators.note: the clue places the comparison word inside the word for bed

parts.note: taken as written
'not as' (much) means less

explanation.surface: A claim that lying in bed leaves you worse off than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In bed' reads as lying down, but 'In' is the container signal; 'is' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone fortunate is favoured by luck, as if divinely favoured.

clue.text: Research scientist leaving home after end of job

indicators.note: the leaving-home pieces come after the letter from job
the end of the word job is its final letter

parts.note: someone leaving is off, as in 'I'm off'
at home means in

explanation.surface: A scientist quitting the house once a job is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a scientist or technical expert, especially in research.

clue.text: Slowly change and pass on responsibility, ignoring leader

indicators.note: ignoring the leader means dropping the opening letter of the synonym

parts.note: to devolve is to hand down duties to a lower level

explanation.surface: Advice about gradual change and delegating, while bypassing the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring leader' trims the first letter from DEVOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to develop gradually over time, as species do.

clue.text: Examine small metal container during voyage at sea

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the container word is put in the middle of the voyage word

parts.note: a cruise is a pleasure voyage on the sea
a tin is a metal can

explanation.surface: Customs inspecting a little tin box on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to look at something closely and in detail.

clue.text: Try to prevent grazing animals crossing top of track

indicators.note: the animals straddle the letter, so it sits within them

parts.note: deer graze on grass

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Stopping deer from wandering onto a country path.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to discourage someone from acting, often through fear of consequences.

clue.text: Opt out in closed event

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit within the word for closed

parts.note: shut means closed

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Choosing not to take part in a closed-door competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opt out' looks like one phrase, but 'out' is the anagram signal for 'Opt' alone; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the shot put is an athletics field event involving throwing a heavy ball.

clue.text: Second family? Mean with money and very clingy

parts.note: kin are one's relatives
tight means stingy

explanation.surface: A miserly relative who is also emotionally possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: skintight clothing fits closely against the body.

clue.text: Love women with education to be outstanding

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Affection for educated women as a route to excellence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' means not yet paid, not excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still unpaid is outstanding, meaning it is due to someone.

clue.text: Indulged in ridiculous pipe dream, with no source of income

indicators.note: ridiculous signals that the letters of the phrase are absurdly jumbled
with no tells us a letter is missing from the jumbled pool
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone lost in a fantasy of wealth with nothing coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (source of income) from PIPEDREAM and rearrange the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pampered means treated with excessive care and comfort.

clue.text: Touching lines created by blokes under effect of the sun

indicators.note: in a down clue the men's word sits below the sun word

parts.note: a tan is skin darkened by sunlight
gents are men

explanation.surface: Sunbathing men forming lines on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Geometry term: lines that meet a curve at one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Defeat hearing defect

indicators.note: hearing signals the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a flaw is a defect

explanation.surface: Losing a court case because of a flaw in the hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent FLAW and FLOOR sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to floor someone is to knock them down or beat them.

clue.text: Society member hears about bishop and valet

indicators.note: the word for hears goes around the letter

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a man is a manservant or valet

explanation.surface: A club member listening to talk of a churchman and his servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribesman belongs to a tribe, a kind of traditional society.

clue.text: Confirmed international tariff will include new event

indicators.note: the letters for the international tariff surround the jumble

parts.note: a rate is a fixed charge or tariff

indicators.note: new signals the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A global trade duty being extended to cover a fresh occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for 'event'; 'will include' wraps the first and last pieces round that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a confirmed habit, like an inveterate smoker, is long established.

clue.text: Time in charge is fair

indicators.note: the time letter sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: A judgement that a period of command has been just.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' is a noun, a village gala, not 'just'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fair is an outdoor festival with stalls and games, like a village gala.

clue.text: Be providing protection for mobile training vessel

indicators.note: the two letters wrap round and shield the jumble
mobile means moving about, so the letters are moved

explanation.surface: Offering security for a portable training programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges TRAINING to RIGANTIN, which BE surrounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a brigantine is a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Pants perhaps turned German off

indicators.note: off suggests the letters have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German put off by underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British for underpants, and 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in British usage pants are underwear, an item worn beneath clothes.

clue.text: EU partner's terrible entrance

indicators.note: a terrible mess of letters is how the rearrangement is signalled

parts.note: the letters of EU and partner, the 's being no letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful way for a fellow European Union member to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' is the verb (en-TRANCE), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to entrance someone is to delight or captivate them.

clue.text: Beat one's opponents crossing ground, but become less convincing

indicators.note: the victory word spans the soil word, holding it inside

parts.note: to beat opponents is to win
earth is ground or soil

explanation.surface: A sporting win on enemy turf whose excuse is getting threadbare.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an excuse that wears thin loses its power to persuade.

clue.text: Unsuitable name, 'Scrooge', when hoarding no millions

indicators.note: the hoarder holds the other letters inside

parts.note: Scrooge is Dickens's archetypal miser

explanation.surface: Calling a penniless hoarder Scrooge is a mismatch.
explanation.definitionFit: A misnomer is a wrong or inaccurate label for something.

clue.text: Plan to go and get X-ray set — it needs reordering

indicators.note: reordering plainly asks for the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Arranging a hospital scan before leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an exit strategy is a planned way of withdrawing from a situation.

clue.text: Cover up a case of these and expand

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lid is a cover

indicators.note: a word's case is its outer letters

explanation.surface: Hiding one of these items and then enlarging it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LID into DIL; the case of 'these' is TE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pupils dilate when they widen or enlarge.

clue.text: Fliers, for example, and engineers test regularly

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of test

explanation.surface: Pilots and engineers running routine trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: egrets are white herons, which are birds that fly.

clue.text: Manage temperature for a little one

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Controlling the heat for a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A runt is the smallest animal of a litter.

clue.text: Out of bed and suffering — honest

parts.note: up means risen from bed
standing something means suffering or tolerating it

explanation.surface: Someone up and in pain who is still truthful.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an upstanding citizen is honourable and respectable.

clue.text: Cat and dog ultimately in row

indicators.note: the dog's letter goes inside the word for row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of dog

explanation.surface: A cat and a dog having a squabble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' is a line of seats, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the tiger is the largest member of the cat family.

clue.text: Mountain within borders of Vietnam

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the country name, between its edges

explanation.surface: A peak inside a south-east Asian country's frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within borders of' means the letters lie inside the country name, not touching its first or last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily.

clue.text: Powerless, being suspended by radio operator

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator
strung means hung up or suspended

explanation.surface: Someone left helpless after being strung up by a radio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hamstrung means crippled or prevented from acting.

clue.text: Silly relation taken in by hollow invective

indicators.note: the relation is placed inside the remaining letters
hollow means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: a nan is a grandmother, a relation

explanation.surface: A foolish relative fooled by empty abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: inane means senseless or foolish.

clue.text: Hurried returns deserve recount

indicators.note: returns means the word for hurried is turned back

parts.note: ran means hurried
to rate something is to deserve it

explanation.surface: Rushed comebacks earning a second tally of votes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns RAN into NAR; 'recount' is to tell, not count again.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to recount a story is to tell it.

clue.text: Errs badly about reversing charge for jackets

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the turned word
badly signals the letters are disordered
reversing means the charge word is read backwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge

explanation.surface: Getting things wrong over a refund on some coats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' is the anagram signal for 'Errs', 'reversing' turns the charge word round, and 'about' puts the jumble around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a reefer is a thick double-breasted jacket of the kind sailors wear.
